title: The Great Emu War
sources: Wikipedia, 'Emu War' (2 Nov to 10 Dec 1932; about 20,000 emus; WWI veterans on marginal wheat land in Western Australia during the Depression asked for machine guns; Major G.P.W. Meredith with two Lewis guns and 10,000 rounds; a gun jammed, a truck-mounted gun could not catch the birds; the emus split into small groups; the army withdrew 8 Nov, returned, and Meredith was recalled 10 Dec; Meredith's report claimed 986 emus from 9,860 rounds, about ten rounds per bird, a figure historians call inflated/disputed; officially a wildlife management operation, the name 'Emu War' came from the media; in 1934 57,034 bounties were claimed in six months)

Scientific American, 'The Great Emu War' (about 20,000 emus wrecking wheat farms in Western Australia; first target a group of about 50 near Campion; a machine gun jammed in the second engagement; emus scattered in all directions and were fast; about ten bullets per emu; in 1934 locals killed 57,034 emus in six months)

lines.text: In 1932, the Australian army went to war with birds.
lines.caps: IN 1932, | THE ARMY WENT | TO WAR WITH | BIRDS

lines.text: Twenty thousand emus were trampling the wheat farms of Western Australia.
The farmers were struggling, and many were World War One veterans, so they asked for machine guns.
The army sent a major, two Lewis guns, and ten thousand rounds.
But emus are fast, and they split into small groups, so the soldiers kept missing.
lines.caps: BUT EMUS | ARE FAST | AND SPLIT UP | SOLDIERS MISSED

lines.text: One gun jammed, and a truck with a gun couldn't even catch them.
lines.caps: ONE GUN | JAMMED | THE TRUCK | COULDN'T CATCH THEM

lines.text: The army pulled out, came back, and pulled out again.
lines.caps: ARMY PULLED OUT | CAME BACK | PULLED OUT AGAIN

lines.text: The major claimed nearly a thousand emus, about ten bullets each.
What finally worked? Bounties. In 1934, farmers claimed over fifty-seven thousand emus.
Officially, it was never even a war, but we all remember who won: the emus.
lines.caps: NEVER A WAR | BUT WE KNOW | WHO WON | THE EMUS
